meta.validation_status: code reviewed by Otto (Q) and numbers accepted by Leo (S), 14 Nov 2026, as reported by ninja for commit 6650ed1; no written sign-off in the repo
meta.frame: MOON_ME planetocentric, east-positive longitude, sphere R = 1737.4 km

files.note: triangle mesh, 2,880,000 triangles, square to 80 S

thresholds.status: project criteria (ninja), not NASA or vehicle limits

method_summary: slope: per-pixel slope from central differences over two pixels in map x and y (baseline 2 px), gradient corrected by the polar stereographic scale factor at the site; statistics over pixel centres inside a disk of the stated ground radius around the site; slopes rounded to 0.01 deg before threshold comparison
DEM: 5 m LOLA GDR where the 2 km disk lies inside it with <= 20 % nodata, else 20 m PGDA ADJ
roughness: RMS height deviation from a least-squares plane over the 100 m landing disk

PSR: zero average Sun visibility in the Mazarico et al. model map; finest map covering the site; The 60 m and 240 m map labels state CENTER_LONGITUDE = 180, the 120 m label and both DEMs 0. Read with lon_0 = 180 (as GDAL parses the label), the 60 m map correlates with the 120 m map at r = -0.05 and with LOLA elevation at r = -0.02 (4000 random points, 85.5-89.5 S); read with lon_0 = 0 it correlates at r = 0.98 and 0.27 (120 m map: 0.28). The 60 m and 240 m maps are therefore read with the DEM's CRS (lon_0 = 0). Leo to confirm.

thermal: Diviner PRP (model-fit annual mean at 2 cm depth and annual maximum surface temperature) of the mesh triangle containing the site; no minimum, no time series, mission-period stability not assessed

status_values.computed: derived here from the named raster
status_values.unknown: data missing or insufficient; see reason

slope.landing_rule: passes the 5 deg slope criterion only if every valid pixel slope in the 100 m radius disk is <= 5.0 deg (AI proposal; Leo decides radius and rule)
slope.source: LDEM_80S_20MPP_ADJ (PGDA product 90, Barker et al. 2023, PSJ 4, 183, doi:10.3847/PSJ/acf3e1; data doi:10.60903/gsfcpgda-lola-spole); MOON_ME (DE421) south polar stereographic, heights relative to 1737.4 km; near field <= 20 km at 20 m/px, far field at 160 m/px (file overview); https://pgda.gsfc.nasa.gov/products/90
slope.method: per-pixel slope from central differences over two pixels in map x and y (baseline 2 px), gradient corrected by the polar stereographic scale factor at the site; statistics over pixel centres inside a disk of the stated ground radius around the site; slopes rounded to 0.01 deg before threshold comparison
limitations: Slope at the DEM's own scale over a 2-pixel baseline; it is not the 100 m point slope in sites.json.
Passing the 5 deg slope criterion alone does not establish overall landing suitability.
A slope fraction over a disk does not establish that a route exists.
site outside the 5 m DEM (87.5-90 S); 20 m DEM used

roughness.measure: RMS height deviation from a least-squares plane, landing disk, DEM pixel scale
roughness.obstacles_reason: features smaller than about two DEM pixels (~40 m on the 20 m DEM), including all boulders, are not resolved; no rock-abundance or boulder map is used
roughness.source: LDEM_80S_20MPP_ADJ (PGDA product 90, Barker et al. 2023, PSJ 4, 183, doi:10.3847/PSJ/acf3e1; data doi:10.60903/gsfcpgda-lola-spole); MOON_ME (DE421) south polar stereographic, heights relative to 1737.4 km; near field <= 20 km at 20 m/px, far field at 160 m/px (file overview); https://pgda.gsfc.nasa.gov/products/90; measure: Shepard et al. 2001, JGR 106(E12), 32777-32795, doi:10.1029/2000JE001429 (RMS height after removing a best-fit plane)
roughness.method: fit z = a x + b y + c to the valid DEM heights inside the landing disk (least squares, ground metres), report sqrt(mean(residual^2))
limitations: DEM heights are interpolated between LOLA tracks; RMS reflects the gridded surface, not metre-scale roughness.
Not a hazard map: obstacles below the detection limit are unknown, not absent.

psr.source: Mazarico et al. 2011, Icarus 211, 1066-1081, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2010.10.030; LOLA PDS average Sun visibility maps AVGVISIB_*_201608 (V1.05, 2016 release); https://pds-geosciences.wustl.edu/lro/lro-l-lola-3-rdr-v1/lrolol_1xxx/extras/illumination/release_2016/img/; 120 m map from the MIT mirror http://imbrium.mit.edu/EXTRAS/ILLUMINATION/IMG/
psr.method: avgvisib_85s_060m_201608.lbl: pixels with DN = 0 grouped into 8-connected clusters; clusters >= 0.1 km2 kept; great-circle distance (R = 1737.4 km) from the site to each kept pixel centre; bearing 0 = north, clockwise; areas use the scale factor at the site
limitations: Shadow = zero average Sun visibility in the Mazarico et al. model map (pixel value exactly 0), not the LROC PSR Atlas.
Permanent shadow is a geometric/thermal condition; it is not evidence of ice.
Proximity is not reachability; the straight line ignores obstacles below the DEM's detection limit, illumination, power, thermal and communication constraints.
Clusters are 8-connected pixels inside a 50 km search box; clusters cut by the box edge are measured only inside it.

roughness.measure: RMS height deviation from a least-squares plane, landing disk, DEM pixel scale
roughness.obstacles_reason: features smaller than about two DEM pixels (~40 m on the 20 m DEM), including all boulders, are not resolved; no rock-abundance or boulder map is used
roughness.source: LDEM_80S_20MPP_ADJ (PGDA product 90, Barker et al. 2023, PSJ 4, 183, doi:10.3847/PSJ/acf3e1; data doi:10.60903/gsfcpgda-lola-spole); MOON_ME (DE421) south polar stereographic, heights relative to 1737.4 km; near field <= 20 km at 20 m/px, far field at 160 m/px (file overview); https://pgda.gsfc.nasa.gov/products/90; measure: Shepard et al. 2001, JGR 106(E12), 32777-32795, doi:10.1029/2000JE001429 (RMS height after removing a best-fit plane)
roughness.method: fit z = a x + b y + c to the valid DEM heights inside the landing disk (least squares, ground metres), report sqrt(mean(residual^2))
limitations: DEM heights are interpolated between LOLA tracks; RMS reflects the gridded surface, not metre-scale roughness.
Not a hazard map: obstacles below the detection limit are unknown, not absent.

psr.source: Mazarico et al. 2011, Icarus 211, 1066-1081, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2010.10.030; LOLA PDS average Sun visibility maps AVGVISIB_*_201608 (V1.05, 2016 release); https://pds-geosciences.wustl.edu/lro/lro-l-lola-3-rdr-v1/lrolol_1xxx/extras/illumination/release_2016/img/; 120 m map from the MIT mirror http://imbrium.mit.edu/EXTRAS/ILLUMINATION/IMG/
psr.method: avgvisib_85s_060m_201608.lbl: pixels with DN = 0 grouped into 8-connected clusters; clusters >= 0.1 km2 kept; great-circle distance (R = 1737.4 km) from the site to each kept pixel centre; bearing 0 = north, clockwise; areas use the scale factor at the site
limitations: Shadow = zero average Sun visibility in the Mazarico et al. model map (pixel value exactly 0), not the LROC PSR Atlas.
Permanent shadow is a geometric/thermal condition; it is not evidence of ice.
Proximity is not reachability; the straight line ignores obstacles below the DEM's detection limit, illumination, power, thermal and communication constraints.
Clusters are 8-connected pixels inside a 50 km search box; clusters cut by the box edge are measured only inside it.
psr.crs_note: The 60 m and 240 m map labels state CENTER_LONGITUDE = 180, the 120 m label and both DEMs 0. Read with lon_0 = 180 (as GDAL parses the label), the 60 m map correlates with the 120 m map at r = -0.05 and with LOLA elevation at r = -0.02 (4000 random points, 85.5-89.5 S); read with lon_0 = 0 it correlates at r = 0.98 and 0.27 (120 m map: 0.28). The 60 m and 240 m maps are therefore read with the DEM's CRS (lon_0 = 0). Leo to confirm.

thermal.source: Paige et al., LRO DLRE LEVEL 5 PRP V2.0, NASA Planetary Data System, LRO-L-DLRE-5-PRP-V2.0, 2018 (citation as given in the PDS catalogue prpds.cat); method: Paige et al. 2010, Science 330(6003), 479 (prpds.cat prints p. 497); https://pds-geosciences.wustl.edu/lro/urn-nasa-pds-lro_diviner_derived1/data_derived_prp/dlre_prp_south.tab
thermal.method: site unit vector tested against the vertices of every mesh triangle whose centre is within 3 km (great circle, R = 1737.4 km); values of the containing triangle; landing-disk statistics over triangle centres within 100 m
limitations: Model-fit values from the first Diviner mapping year (Paige et al. 2010 method), per the label: temp_avg = annual average at 2 cm depth, temp_max = annual maximum at the surface.
Not an annual minimum, not a time series and not a value for the mission dates: thermal stability over the mission period is NOT assessed.
One mesh triangle (about 0.1-0.2 km2, Kaguya-derived DEM) is larger than the 100 m landing disk; sub-triangle slopes and shadows are averaged out.
Frame: label says Moon-centered (planetocentric, east-positive, R = 1737.4 km); read as MOON_ME, confirmed by Leo (S) on 14 Nov 2026.
temp_max_k minus temp_avg_k is not a temperature range (different depths and statistics); no range is given.
The ice_depth column (model ice-stability depth) is not used; no ice is inferred.
Sun visibility is not used as a temperature proxy.
thermal.terms: public NASA PDS data; no licence or usage terms in the .lbl or .xml; NASA SMD policy SPD-41a requires SMD-funded scientific information to be made publicly available (https://science.nasa.gov/researchers/science-data/science-information-policy/); cite the product as below

temp_avg.description: The annual average temperature (K), calculated at a depth of 2 cm below the surface

temp_max.description: The annual maximum temperature (K), calculated at the surface

landing_area.note: mesh is coarser than the landing area: at most one triangle centre lies within 100 m, so no landing-area statistics
